title: Probation Surcharge on a Cancellation Refund — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
The probation surcharge is booked on a policy under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) for each term the community is on NFIP probation; this entry settles how much of it a cancellation refund returns.

**Earned and returned.** For a cancellation refund whose current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit, each counted by its risk premium entries, and only for such a refund, the probation surcharge of a term that began after the cancellation took effect is returned in full, while that of the term in which a cancellation under current term full or pro rata takes effect stays fully earned; for a cancellation refund whose terms carry more than one premium-bearing endorsement or more than one re-rate credit, the probation surcharge is fully earned under current term full and pro rata.

**Rule.** The probation surcharge a cancellation refund returns is settled as follows: when the reason refunds from inception, the probation surcharges of the current term and the term before it; when the cancellation took effect before the current term start, the current term's probation surcharge in full; otherwise none.

A reason refunds from inception when it is a duplicate NFIP policy or a loan closing that did not occur.

## Judgement points

- Inception reasons return the current and preceding terms' probation surcharges.
- A cancellation effective before the current term start returns the current term's surcharge in full; the preceding term's stays earned.
- A cancellation effective on or after the current term start returns none.
- A term in which no probation surcharge was booked returns none, because nothing was charged.
